la:noun:favonius.html:
Făvōnĭus, ii, m.
faveo
.
The west wind, also called Zephyrus, which blew at the commencement of spring, and promoted vegetation, ; ; ; ; ; ; ; ; —
Deriv.: † făvōnĭālis, Ζεφύριος, Gloss. Philox.—
A Roman proper name. So esp. M. Favonius, a contemporary of Cicero and an imitator of M. Cato, whence he received the derisive sobriquet of simius Catonis, ; ; ; ; . —
Deriv.: Făvōnĭānus, a, um, adj., of or belonging to a Favonius, Favonian: pira,; .

la:verb:faveo.gloss: to be favorable, to be well disposed or inclined towards, to favor, promote, befriend, countenance, protect
senses: to be favorable, to be well disposed or inclined towards, to favor, promote, befriend, countenance, protect
to countenance, applaud, support, encourage, indulge
la:verb:faveo.html:
făvĕo, fāvi, fautum, 2, v. n.
perh. root φαϝ-, φάος, φῶς, light, safety; cf. also foveo
,
to be favorable, to be well disposed or inclined towards, to favor, promote, befriend, countenance, protect (class.; syn.: studeo, foveo, diligo, amo).
In gen.
With dat.: favere et cupere Helvetiis propter eam affinitatem (opp. odisse),: qui diligebant hunc, illi favebant,; cf. favor, II.: ille (chorus) bonis faveatque et consilietur amice (= semper cum personis probis stet),: Romanis Juno coepit placata favere, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 289 ed. Vahl.): tibi favemus, te tuā frui virtute cupimus, etc.,: rescripsi ... me ei fauturum,: non multo plus patriae faveo quam tuae gloriae,: rei publicae, dignitati ac gloriae tuae,: nostrae laudi dignitatique,: huic meae voluntati,; cf.: honori et dignitati,: sententiae,: rebus Gallicis,: rebus Caesaris,: favere et plaudere ingeniis sepultis, 2, 1, 88: operi, et saep.: honoribus,: huc coëamus ait ... Coëamus retulit Echo, et verbis favet ipsa suis,i. e. delights in,: qui (galli) silentio noctis, ut ait Ennius, favent faucibus russis cantu,i. e. give rest to, indulge,.—Pass. impers.: non modo non invidetur illi aetati, verum etiam favetur,; so, favetur,; : huic Romae ita fautum est, ut, etc., Spartian. Pescenn. 2.—
Absol. (very rare; mostly poet. and in post-Aug. prose): maxime favet judex qui, etc.,; cf.: judices, ut faveant, rogamus,: si favet alma Pales,: assis, o Tegeaee, favens (= propitius),: Phoebe, fave,: faveas, Cypria,; cf.: quisquis es, o faveas,: vos, o, coetum, Tyrii, celebrate faventes,: favente Marte,; cf.: faventibus diis,: et bonos et aequos et faventes vos habui dominos,.—
With inf. (= cupere): matronae moeros complent spectare faventes, Enn. ap. (Ann. v. 376 ed. Vahl., but not in , v. Loers. ad h. l.).—
Of inanim. subjects: (terra) altera frumentis favet, altera Baccho, densa magis Cereri, etc.,is favorable, promotes,: dum favet nox,: venti faventes (i. q. secundi, prosperi),favorable,.
In partic.
In relig. lang., linguis, rarely linguā, ore, etc., to speak good words or to abstain from evil words (the Greek εὐφημεῖν); hence, to keep still, be silent: idcirco rebus divinis, quae publice fierent, ut FAVERENT LINGVIS imperabatur; inque feriis imperandis, ut LITIBVS ET IVRGIIS SE ABSTINERENT,; cf.: faventia bonam ominationem significat. Nam praecones clamantes populum sacrificiis FAVERE jubebant. Favere enim est bona fari: at veteres poëtae pro silere usi sunt favere, Paul. ex Fest. s. v. faventia. p. 88, 6 Müll.: vidimus certis precationibus custodem praeponi, qui faveri linguis jubeat,; : prospera lux oritur: linguis animisque favete; Nunc dicenda bono sunt bona verba die,; cf.: dicamus bona verba, venit natalis, ad aras. Quisquis ades, linguā vir mulierque fave,: en deus est, deus est! linguis animisque favete, quisquis ades! dixit ... Quisquis adest, jussum veneratur numen, et omnes Verba sacerdotis referunt geminata,: contecti gladiis sub scutis ore faventes (= tacentes), Enn. ap. Phil. (Ann. v. 415 ed. Vahl.); cf.: ore favete omnes et cingite tempora ramis,: odi profanum vulgus et arceo. Favete linguis,: quoties mentio sacra litterarum intervenerit, favete linguis,: sacra facit vates? sint ora faventia sacris, cf.: concipiamque bonas ore favente preces,: linguā favens assit (diei natali), longorum oblita malorum,; ; cf.: mente favete pari, etc.,.—Absol.: favete (= tacete), adeste aequo animo et rem cognoscite,.—
To applaud: quo clamor vocat et turba faventium, etc.,; cf.: tum clamore, qualis ex insperato faventium solet, Romani adjuvant militem suum (Horatium),: infensus turbae faventi adversus studium suum,; : tu Veneri dominae plaude favente manu,.

la:noun:favilla.html:
făvilla, ae, f.
Sanscr. root bhā-, to shine; Gr. φα-, φῶς, etc., cf. Lat. fax
,
hot cinders or ashes, glowing ashes, embers (cf. cinis).
Lit. (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): ibi favillae plena coquendo sit faxo (psaltria). : scintillas agere ac late differre favillam,; cf. ; and: cum contectus ignis ex se favillam discutit scintillamque emittit,: candens,: cana,: e carbone restincto favilla digito sublata,: cinis e favilla et carbonibus ad calefaciendum triclinium illatus,: nihil invenit praeter tepidam in ara favillam,: vi pulveris ae favillae oppressus est. (Plinius), Suet. Fragm. Hist., ed. Roth, p. 301.—
In partic., the ashes of the dead still glowing: corporis favillam ab reliquo separant cinere,: ibi tu calentem Debita sparges lacrima favillam Vatis amici,; ; ; ; .—
Transf.: salis,powder of salt,.—*
Trop., a glimmering spark, i. e. beginning, origin: haec est venturi prima favilla mali,.

la:noun:favor.html:
făvor, ōris, m.
id.
,
favor, good-will, inclination, partiality, esp. of a party (rare in Cic.; not in Caes.; freq. since the Aug. per. in prose and poetry; syn.: studium, benevolentia, gratia, pietas, caritas, amor).
In gen.
Of human beings: favorem et urbanum Cicero nova credit. Nam in epistola ad Brutum, Eum, inquit, amorem et eum (ut hoc verbo utar) favorem in consilium advocabo,; so with amor,; with studium,: qui favore populi tenetur et ducitur,; cf. under II.: quae sunt varie et ad tempus descripta populis, favore magis quam re, legum nomen tenent,: amplecti aliquem favore,: adferre alicui,: ex maxima invidia in gratiam et favorem nobilitatis Jugurtha venit,; cf. opp. invidia,: plebis,; cf. : partium Pompeii,: concilia to populi favore,: militum,; ; : favor in aliquem,: pro laborantibus,. —
Rarely of Fortune: fortunae favor,; .—
Favor personified as a deity, —
Esp., legal t. t.: favoris causa, said where the law inclines to or encourages a particular right or practice: hoc favoris causa constitutum est, ut pro plenis (honoribus) incoätos accipiamus,; ; Gai ; cf.: favor libertatis,; sq.—
In partic., acclamation, applause, at theatrical and other exhibitions (syn. plausus), approbation: quod studium et quem favorem secum in scenam attulit Panurgus?; : audientium,: facere favorem,: promere favorem,: emerendi favoris gratia,: magno omnium favore,; cf.: plauditur et magno palma favore datur,: tutatur favor Euryalum,.

la:noun:favus.html:
făvus, i, m.,
a honey-comb.
Prop.: favus est, quem fingunt (apes) multicavatum e cera, cum singula cava sena latera habeant,; ; ; ; ; ; : mellis, et saep.—Prov.: Crescere tamquam favum,i. e. imperceptibly, and 76.—
Transf., a hexagonal stone in a pavement, .

la:noun:favea.html:
făvĕa, ae, f.
faveo
,
